name: IL-05
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Mike Quigley running with large cash advantage
Republican challenger has reported no fundraising
Prediction markets price Democratic win at ~98%
model.rationale: Quigley holds a heavily Democratic Chicago-area seat with a $1.2 million war chest, while Tommy Hanson shows no reported fundraising or outside support. Markets price a Democratic win near certainty, and fundamentals point to a margin in the mid-20s.
model.watch: Any unexpected Quigley scandal or retirement, or a late surge of outside spending for Hanson, could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Mike Quigley seeks another term in this Chicago-based district, which leans Democratic by about 19 points. He enters the general election with roughly $1.2 million on hand after raising over $725,000, while Republican Tommy Hanson reports no fundraising and draws no outside spending on either side. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Quigley's chances near 98 percent.

The fundamentals point to a comfortable Democratic margin in the mid-20s, consistent with the district's lean, the incumbent's advantages, and a favorable national environment. Barring an unforeseen development, this race is not expected to be competitive.
